name: Heart Free Pham

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB questionnaire, Pham said he would introduce hemp blocks to create more affordable, sustainable housing.
positions.excerpt: I would introduce the use of hemp (more specifically hemp blocks) to create more affordable, sustainable housing.

positions.statement: In a 2024 KATU questionnaire on homelessness, Pham said he would build a coalition with surrounding cities, counties and advocacy groups.
positions.excerpt: Build a coalition with surrounding cities, counties, and advocacy groups

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB questionnaire, Pham said only $300,000 of cannabis tax revenue was allocated to drug and alcohol treatment.
positions.excerpt: only $300,000 was allocated towards drug/alcohol treatment.

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB questionnaire, Pham said he prioritizes road surfacing over bike lanes, saying biking to work is a privilege of the wealthy.
positions.excerpt: biking to work is a privilege of the wealthy

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB questionnaire, Pham objected to using PCEF funds for city fleet electrification, saying the city is on pace to use 99% renewable diesel by 2030.
positions.excerpt: This doesn't make sense to me as the city is already on pace to use 99% renewable diesel by 2030.

positions.statement: In a 2024 OPB questionnaire, Pham said he wants the Small Donor Elections program eliminated, saying taxpayers should not subsidize candidates' political aspirations.
positions.excerpt: taxpayers shouldn't be subsidizing the political aspirations of anyone that chooses to run for office

positions.statement: In a 2024 KOIN questionnaire, Pham said housing and health care are human rights.
positions.excerpt: Housing is a human right, health care is a human right.

collection_notes: Campaign site fetch returned only a page title. 2024-cycle KATU, OPB and KOIN questionnaires used per coordinator instruction, each dated in its statement. Identity: same name and same office/district; 2024 pages describe a 34-year-old railroad conductor born and raised in Portland, consistent with the 2026 Portland Mercury bio. Quotes are partial because WebFetch caps quotes. The 6 earlier 2026-framed searches found nothing; remaining unmatched issues gapped (not searched, low coverage). Public-safety questionnaire answer (police hiring) had no quotable verbatim passage, so it is gapped.
